note: Adapted from the species description in Emerson (1928). The original is in English; soldier and alate are treated, but the alate is represented only by comparative remarks and has no full description, so only the soldier is included. Workers are not recorded. Figure numbers, localities, derivation of the name and field observations are omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate with a relatively large ocellus, separated from the compound eye by only one-sixth of its diameter; M. lounsburyi is smaller and closely related; M. vadschaggae has a smaller ocellus; M. thoracalis has a smaller ocellus and the sides of the posterior part of the pronotum straighter. Soldier somewhat similar to variety depauperata of M. subhyalinus, but the latter has twelve-segmented antennae; the head of M. subhyalinus is proportionally shorter; M. pusillus has twelve-segmented antennae.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head yellow, densely covered with short hairs; sides rounded, converging anteriorly. Antennae 13-segmented, third segment smaller than fourth, fourth smaller than second. Labrum long, distinctly exceeding half the length of the mandibles. Mandibles dark reddish brown, yellow at base. Anterior margin of pronotum deeply concave. Fore tibia inflated. Head length 1.22–1.27 mm; head width 0.64–0.73 mm; antennal length 1.05 mm; pronotum 0.33 mm long, 0.47–0.50 mm wide; hind tibia 0.58 mm long; left mandible 0.56 mm long.
